notes.n8.framework: Open-source, developer-led; every frontier lab and hyperscaler now ships its own agent SDK (OpenAI, Google ADK, Claude Agent SDK, AWS Strands, Microsoft Agent Framework) alongside independents LangChain (US$1.25B valuation, Oct 2025), LlamaIndex and CrewAI.
notes.n8.vector: Standalone vector DBs (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus/Zilliz, Chroma) compete with vector features in incumbent databases (Postgres/pgvector, MongoDB, Elastic, Redis, Oracle); retrieval models are being folded into search incumbents (Elastic-Jina, MongoDB-Voyage).
notes.n8.ingest: Two clusters: document parsing/OCR (Unstructured, Reducto, LlamaParse, Docling, Mistral OCR) and web-to-LLM search/crawl APIs (Tavily, Exa, Parallel, Firecrawl); the latter is consolidating into AI clouds (Nebius-Tavily ~US$275M, Feb 2026).
notes.n8.memory: Early, venture-funded and mostly open-source (Mem0, Letta, Zep, Cognee); hyperscalers now bundle managed memory (e.g. AWS AgentCore Memory) and vector-DB vendors are repositioning as memory layers.
notes.n8.tools: MCP became the de facto tool-integration standard and moved to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (Dec 2025); value is shifting to auth-aware connector platforms (Composio, Arcade) and integration incumbents (Workday-Pipedream, Zapier, Workato).
notes.n8.sandbox: Two segments: code-execution sandboxes (E2B, Modal, Daytona, Vercel) and cloud browsers for web agents (Browserbase, Browser Use, Kernel); hyperscalers (AWS AgentCore, Cloudflare) now offer both natively.
notes.n8.platform: Dominated by data platforms (Databricks, Snowflake), hyperscaler agent platforms and application incumbents (Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP), with Palantir AIP as the leading independent; China served by Baidu, Alibaba and ByteDance clouds.
notes.n8.lowcode: Crowded: open-source builders (n8n at US$2.5B, Oct 2025; Dify; Flowise and Langflow now owned by Workday and IBM) vs. suite builders (Copilot Studio, OpenAI Agent Builder, Gemini Enterprise, Agentforce) and automation incumbents (Zapier, Make, UiPath, Workato).
notes.n8.payments: Protocol race in 2025-26: OpenAI/Stripe ACP (Sep 2025), Google AP2 (Sep 2025) and UCP (Jan 2026), Visa Trusted Agent Protocol, Mastercard Agent Pay and Coinbase/Cloudflare x402; agent identity is being absorbed by IAM incumbents (Okta, Microsoft Entra, Twilio-Stytch, PANW-CyberArk).
notes.n8.cache: Thin as a standalone market: semantic caching is mostly a feature of gateways and databases (Redis LangCache, Cloudflare, Portkey, GPTCache) and prompt optimisation is led by open-source DSPy.
notes.n8.eval: Voice-agent evaluation (Coval, Hamming, Cekura) has emerged as a distinct sub-niche.
notes.n8.security: Fastest-consolidating sub-segment: in about 15 months, Palo Alto (Protect AI), Check Point (Lakera), SentinelOne (Prompt Security), F5 (CalypsoAI), Cato (Aim), CrowdStrike (Pangea), Zscaler (SPLX), Snyk (Invariant), Tenable (Apex), Proofpoint (Acuvity) and OpenAI (Promptfoo) bought startups; agent-security independents (Zenity, Noma, HiddenLayer) raised US$100M+ rounds.
notes.n8.gov: Pure-play AI governance vendors (Credo AI, Holistic AI, Saidot, Trustible) compete with GRC/privacy suites (OneTrust, Securiti-Veeam, Collibra) and platform-embedded governance (IBM watsonx.governance, ServiceNow AI Control Tower); demand is driven by EU AI Act and ISO 42001.
notes.n8.orch: Control-plane race among enterprise platforms (Microsoft Agent 365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Workday, IBM, AWS); open registries via MCP Registry and A2A Agent Cards.
notes.n8.search: Consolidating fast after Microsoft retired Bing Search APIs (Aug 2025): Nebius bought Tavily, Elastic bought Jina; Exa ($2.2B) and Parallel ($2B) lead independents.
notes.n8.identity: Incumbent IAM is buying in (Palo Alto-CyberArk, Cisco-Astrix, Twilio-Stytch) while Okta and Microsoft ship agent-native identity; Israeli NHI startups prominent.
